name: Headless label in the browser identity
plain: The browser's name tag can say it is running without a screen.
meaning: Headless Chrome announces itself as HeadlessChrome in the User-Agent string and in the Sec-CH-UA brand list unless the operator overrides it. Bot defenses read it first. Agents that patch the user agent often forget the client hint brands, so the two disagree and give the agent away.

steps: Browser sends User-Agent and Sec-CH-UA on every request
Server or page script reads the brand names
Compare the label with the other headers and the JavaScript values

firefox.note: Headless Firefox sends the normal user agent

fields.name: Sec-CH-UA
fields.range: brand list that may include HeadlessChrome

fields.name: userAgentData.brands
fields.range: same brands as the header when not patched

limits.headline: Can show that Chrome is running without a visible window
limits.user_action: Nothing. It is sent with every request
can: Read the browser name and brand list
Compare the user agent with client hints to find patched agents
Block or challenge clients that look headless
cannot: Tell a real person from a well disguised agent
See what the script is doing
Stop operators from changing the label
limits.reach_label: A name tag the operator can rewrite
limits.differs: Operators change it with one launch flag, so a clean label proves little. A mismatch between the user agent and the client hints is the stronger clue.

story.what_it_is: Headless Chrome tells every site it has no window, in the same place it states its name and version.

marketing.name: Headless Chrome
marketing.pitch: Docs describe running Chrome without a visible UI for automation and testing.

story.for_you: You never see it. Your normal browser reports its plain name. If you run an agent in headless mode, some sites challenge it on arrival.
story.for_makers: It is the cheapest headless check and sits at the network layer, before any script runs. Check that the user agent string, the Sec-CH-UA brands and navigator.userAgentData all agree.

use_cases.example: A firewall serves a challenge to any request whose brand list says HeadlessChrome.
A ticket seller drops queue requests from headless browsers.
An ad network does not count views from clients that report a headless brand.
A site analytics tool files headless visits under bots.
A tester sees the label in server logs and knows the run was headless.
A fare site hides prices from clients that announce headless mode.

technical_bounds: Trivially rewritten with a launch flag
A patched user agent with unpatched client hints is the stronger tell

history.change: Headless mode ships and sends a HeadlessChrome user agent
New headless mode shares the full browser code but keeps the HeadlessChrome label by default
